Right printed page: only a narrow strip at the right edge of the scan, its text cut off by the edge, so the lines are fragments.

main_text.p: nobis postulat,lex n. à nobis postulat aut per- fectâ obedietiâ,aut pœnâ nos a. perfectâ obe- dientiâ non præstitimus, at pœnam luimus in Christo;is n. ꝓ nobis luit,ergo legi satisfeci- mus in Christo : hæc dicunt illi, qui exclude- re volunt iustitiam & sanctificationem Christi ab ecclesia; nec intelligunt quam dissoluras scopas adferant. Si quis intelligat sensum su- perioris sententiæ is hic erit. Præditi ea iusti- tia q̄ lex postulat, tantummodo luuat pœnam illam quam minatur lex. At, ô bone vir, hoc non est præditum esse iustitia quam postulat lex, vt pœnam tantummodo luas. Nam iusti- tia, est legis obedientia, non pœna legis. Pœ- na iniustis ponitur, nō autem iustis. Pœna igi- tur est iniustitiæ argumentum non autem iu- stitiæ. Apostolus docet nos legis iustitiam im- plere: tu exponis ea verba, nos præditos esse legis iustitia. Iustidam implere, & iusticia præ- ditum esse, non significat iniustum esse, aut reputari: at pœnam legis luere, significat in- iustum reputari: hæc non cohærent.

Deinde, ꝙ Christus pœnam luerit pro no- bis, quis potest negare, nisi qui Christum ne- gat? nos igitur virtutem mortis Christi non negamus, at quare eā virtutem iustitiæ Christi negas? Nam sicut Christus ꝓ nobis pœnā luit, sic ꝓ nobis etiam obedientiā perfectam præ- stitit. Nos inquis, obedientiam perfectam, q̄ lex postulat, non præstitimus, at pœnam lui- mus in Christo, quia ille ꝓ nobis luit. Respon- deo : ille etiam pro nobis perfectam obedien-

page.notes: Left column is complete; the last line ends on a broken word, "obedien-", with the catchword "tiam" below. The marks (,,) down the left edge are printer's marks, not text, and are not transcribed. "Iustidam" and "luuat" are printed as they stand, so they may be printing errors. "tia q̄" and "ꝙ" stand for abbreviations for quam and quod and are read from the scan. Right printed page: only a cropped strip survives at the right edge. Its lines are fragments, several with [?] unread. The page number, running head and any catchword of the right page are not visible.
